# powsimR

## Role

powsimR supports a priori and posterior power analysis for bulk and single-cell
RNA-seq differential-expression experiments. The supplied vignette describes
fitting mean-dispersion and, where relevant, dropout relationships from a
reference count matrix, simulating counts under chosen DE effects/sample sizes,
and evaluating error rates across analysis choices.

## simitall Position

Use as an optional study-design and power-analysis layer. SimItAll retains its
own causal expression/eQTL truth and can compare powsimR-style power summaries
with its standard validation tables.

## Inputs

- A suitable reference count matrix or an explicitly synthetic count model.
- Sample-size grid, effect-size/DE prevalence assumptions, and analysis methods.
- For single-cell data: cell type, donor/batch design, and dropout assumptions.

## Outputs and Validation

- Simulated count sets, power/false-discovery summaries, and error-rate plots
  across sample sizes and effect sizes.
- Treat estimated reference distributions as dataset-specific, not universal.

## Guardrails

- Fit reference parameters within a biologically coherent group; do not pool
  incompatible cell types, conditions, or batches merely to increase size.
- Power conclusions depend on the assumed effect distribution and analysis
  pipeline and should be shown as sensitivity analyses.

## Tutorial Provenance

Curated from user-supplied `powsimR • powsimR.html`, which cites Vieth et al.
(2017), *Bioinformatics*, DOI: 10.1093/bioinformatics/btx435.
